newsitem.title: DUBAI: UAE to penalise banks which don't employ nationals.
newsitem.headline: UAE to penalise banks which don't employ nationals.

text.p: A special United Arab Emirates committee has proposed stiff penalties for banks which do not meet planned new laws to raise the number of UAE nationals among bank staff, the commitee's chairman said in published remarks.

UAE Communications Minister Ahmad Humaid al-Tayer, who is also head of the body reviewing national staffing levels at banks, was quoted by the daily Gulf News on Wednesday as saying compulsory measures to implement the prosposed state policy would be introduced soon.
"Tayer said the 12-member committee...(was) not convinced with the results of their 14-month campaign to increase the percentage of nationals in banks voluntarily," the paper said.
It said the number of nationals working at banks rose by 0.4 percent last year compared to the targetted four percent rise.

A draft law calling for an increase in the number of UAE nationals in banks to 50 percent in 10 years is being referred to the cabinet for approval, Tayer said. The law will stipulate banks increase their national workforce by four percent a year.
UAE nationals currently account for nine percent of bank staff.
Tayer said the proposed law would impose "tough measures on banks to achieve targets or face tough penalties including freezing of applications for new branches or additional expatriate employees".
The UAE, like most Gulf Arab states, is trying to find more jobs for its citizens to reduce reliance on expatriate labour.
About three quarters of the 2.4 million people in the UAE are foreigners -- most of them from the Indian subcontinent and southeast Asia.
